subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - next steps

Subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - post-call recap

Hi Sam —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps for the POC/trial: 

Summary of objectives
- Primary goal: validate low-latency customer-facing generation for support bot (95th perc latency < 300ms for typical queries)
- Success criteria: latency, token-cost per request under target, model quality judged by 4 curated prompt categories, and throughput for concurrent users (~50 rps during peak)

Evaluation plan & timeline (proposed)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and pick environment option (hosted trial, dedicated sandbox, or VPC trial)
- Week 1-2: environment setup + smoke tests (connection + auth + sample prompts)
- Week 3: scale tests + quality evaluation with your prompt set
- Week 4: readout and decision / next steps

Environment options we discussed
1) Hosted (fastest): Redwood hosted trial with dedicated project and sample data. Pros: fastest onboarding (~1 business day), no infra changes. Cons: data routing through Redwood-hosted infra.
2) Dedicated sandbox: reserved capacity on our hosted fleet for your tests; predictable throughput, data isolated within the tenant. Pros: better performance guarantees, similar onboarding (2-3 days).
3) VPC trial: private connectivity (VPC peering / private link) with customer-managed network for strict data controls. Pros: meets stricter security/compliance needs. Cons: networking setup and firewall config required (typically 1-2 weeks).

Immediate asks / owners
- Sam: confirm preferred environment option (hosted / dedicated sandbox / VPC) and the internal owner for network setup if choosing VPC
- Alex: please share the evaluation prompt set (sample 30-50 prompts) and expected concurrency profile
- Rishi / Dev (cc'd): will provide network checklist, test account details, and a POC checklist PDF.

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (POC runbook), network-requirements-template.xlsx

Proposed next step: If you confirm environment preference by end of week, we can schedule a kickoff and have a baseline environment ready early next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC - network & infra checklist

Hi Alex / Sam —

Thanks for confirming VPC. Below are the high-level network and infra items we need to enable a VPC trial. I attached a template (network-requirements-template.xlsx) to make it easier.

Network checklist (high level)
- Private connectivity: VPC peering or PrivateLink; we prefer PrivateLink for smaller config surface but we can support either.
- Inbound/outbound firewall rules: allow outbound to our control plane IPs (listed in the attachment) and open necessary ports (TLS 443).
- DNS: optional private DNS or split-horizon setup if you need to resolve model endpoints internally.
- Static egress IPs: if you require allowlists on your side, confirm current egress IPs.
- Certificate / mTLS: if you want mutual auth, we can enable mTLS (requires cert exchange).

POC environment options (technical tradeoffs)
- Hosted with VPC-connect: fastest (1-2 business days) - Redwood-managed runtime but network traffic goes over PrivateLink to your VPC.
- Dedicated sandbox + VPC: reserved capacity inside a tenant with PrivateLink - better for predictable throughput and isolation (3-7 business days to provision depending on approvals).
- Full private deployment (on-prem/VPC self-managed): longest lead time (>2 weeks), only needed for strict regulatory constraints.

Please provide the following to get started:
1) Contact for network engineer who can accept a 30-45 min kickoff call (Alex?)
2) The prompt set and a small sample payloads (JSON) to validate request/response shapes
3) Any allowlist / firewall details (IPs) and whether you need mTLS

Next steps: once Alex confirms a time for the network kickoff we'll schedule an internal provisioning window. I attached the network template and included our control-plane IPs and PrivateLink endpoint info.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.ai
